# E1-v5 — the headline three-way comparison on clean files (packaging v5, prompt version 4)

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** stopped 4 Oct — superseded by E1-v6

> **Not the current result.** This question is answered by [E1-v6 — the headline three-way comparison on clean files in TSVC's own form (packaging v6, prompt version 4)](../E01v6_clean_files_three_way/REPORT.md); this folder is kept as history. See [`results/README.md`](../README.md).

## The question

E1-final again where the file a model reads is an ordinary code file (the loop's function alone, no note, no harness, one editable file) and the order statement is the corrected one: on TSVC class R (with class A and D controls), DiscoPoP alone vs the Haiku agent vs Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable alone — who ships correct, race-free, faster programs, and who ships unusable ones?

## Result in one paragraph

Stopped by the author after 8 trials (none analysed): in packaging v5 the function is one repetition, called 48 times, and a temporary array obtained inside it is paid on every call (T0.17). The same experiment runs on packaging v6 as E1-v6.

| 2026-10-04 | deviation | **E1-v5 stopped by the author's objection (20:10 UTC) — no trial is analysed.** After the costs of the clean layout were put to the author (the function compiled alone; a temporary array created on each of the 48 calls; a lower best-achievable speedup), the author: "I do not like that this solution make the speed up worse", then "The best achievable speedup is lower is a problem ans the tmp array is alos a problem". This replaces the decision of the row below ("the model's decision", option A): a cost the LAYOUT adds to a temporary array is not accepted. **Stopped:** the Mac queue (4 of 22 launches made); the four running jobs `e1v5_r_1`, `e1v5_r_2`, `e1v5_r_3`, `e1v5_r_4`, killed on the server with 0, 1, 4 and 3 trials finished; credential sweep clean. The eight finished trials are archived under `results/E01v5_clean_files_three_way/superseded/` and enter no analysis — nothing of them has been read. `e1v5_a`, `e1v5_d`, `e1v5_bare_haiku`, `e1v5_bare_sonnet`, `e1v5_bare_opus`, `e1v5_bare_fable` and `e1v5_race_check` were never launched. **A statement of mine that has to be checked before it is repeated:** "the ceiling in this layout is lower (median 2.98× against 4.10×)" set two different measurements side by side — T0.10 timed the one-file packaging with 12 threads free to use a whole idle node (`tsvc_ceiling.py --pin 1`), `t0_14_c1_refs` timed the clean one on one 12-core lane. Loop by loop at the same size the SEQUENTIAL times agree and the parallel reference is 20–35 % slower in the clean layout on the loops bound by memory traffic, class A loops with one pragma and no temporary array among them (`s000` 0.640 → 0.812 s, `vpvtv` 0.892 → 1.205 s), while `s255`, `s292`, `s281` are unchanged; and the compiled parallel loop of `s000` is the same vector code in both layouts (read from the object files, Mac, clang 19). That pattern is what a busy neighbouring lane would give and not what the layout would give — so whether the ceiling is lower at all is open. **Owed now, no model:** (1) both packagings' references timed alike — one lane, the other lanes idle, interleaved loop by loop; (2) a package form in which a temporary array is paid once, as it was when the repetition loop was inside the function (E1-final's archived programs: where a model alone or the agent allocated a temporary array, it did so BEFORE the repetition loop in 33 of 33 agent programs, 42 of 42 Sonnet, 30 of 30 Opus, 34 of 34 Fable, 24 of 39 Haiku) — measured before it is proposed; then the author decides, and the pre-registration is rewritten for what is decided | The author, 4 Oct |
| 2026-10-04 | finding | **E1-v5's smoke run (`e1v5_smoke`, 12 trials, 10 model calls, $1.41 API-equivalent; never counted): the configuration works — and it shows a cost of the layout that has to be decided before the main runs.** Every trial changed the benchmark's file only, no scaffold problem, no failed call, the hot loop found. `s000`: FASTER in all six set-ups (3.4–3.7×). `s211`: DiscoPoP alone no change; the Haiku agent a correct split with one loop left sequential (1.04×, parallel-not-faster); Haiku alone BROKEN; **Sonnet alone and Opus alone the correct split, 0.64× and 0.95×; Fable alone the same split, 2.2× (FASTER)**. Why (read from the programs, then measured on the server at LARGE, 12 threads, original 1.37 s): Sonnet's and Opus's programs `malloc` their scratch array inside the function and `free` it again; the function is called once per repetition, 48 times, and glibc serves a block of this size by a fresh mapping every time — every element page-faults anew, which costs more than the loop: 1.89 s and 1.98 s. Fable keeps the array in a `static` pointer: 0.61 s. With the allocator told to keep freed memory (`MALLOC_MMAP_MAX_=0`, `MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_` large, `MALLOC_TOP_PAD_`), the SAME two programs run in 0.66 s and 0.74 s (2.07×, 1.85×) and Fable's in 0.64 s. In v4 this cost did not exist: the function ran once per program, a buffer was allocated once. So in the clean layout "FASTER" also asks whether a program keeps its scratch memory between calls — which no arm is told, and which the agent can learn from its speed check while the model alone cannot. **The decision, the author's, before any main trial:** (A) leave it — the result then measures restructuring AND scratch-memory handling; (B) run every program with the allocator keeping freed memory, in the harness's verification and the agent's speed check alike — a property of how programs are run (a known glibc tuning), the same for the original and every candidate, no file and no prompt changed; (C) tell every arm that the function is called repeatedly (a prompt change). Recommended: B. Built as a switch, OFF until decided (`harness_include.KEEP_FREED_MEMORY`; each run's manifest records `allocator_env`). The references are unaffected (their scratch array is `static`). **Two checks of B, before it is offered:** every stage of the agent's gate builds the environment of the program it runs from the process's own (`timing.py`, `schedules.py`, `patching.py`, the profiling runner), so the agent's speed check and the harness's verification run under the same allocator; and the sequential ORIGINAL under both settings (server, lane 1.1, median of 3): `s211` LARGE 1.371 s and 1.363 s, `s000` EXTRALARGE 2.933 s and 2.931 s — it runs at the largest size with every array on the heap, the digest identical —, but `k19` LARGE 2.283 s and 2.440 s (+7 %) and `s244` EXTRALARGE 8.76 s and 8.03 s (−8 %): where the arrays lie changes, and with it the original's time on some loops by a few per cent; a speedup is the ratio of two runs under the SAME setting. E1-v5's expectation that the models alone would be at E1-final's level was written before this run and stands as written | Finding, smoke run |

The population, the models, N, the threads, the tests are E1-final's. **Population** — classes measured on the new packages (`t0_11_c1_a`–`t0_11_c1_c`, every loop the same in 3 of 3), sizes measured on them (`t0_1_c1_sizes`): class R × 5 — s112, s121, s1213, s127, s211, s212, s241, s243, s244, s252, s254, s255, s281, s291, s292, s293, s331, s341; class A × 1 — s000, vpvtv, s313; class D × 3 — s321, s322, s323, s3112: 105 trials per setup. **Runs** (registered in `results/campaign.json`, group E1-v5): the agent and DiscoPoP alone (`default_v4`, `discopop_gate_v4`, Haiku) on class R in four runs on the four 12-core lanes — `e1v5_r_1` (s112 s121 s1213 s127 s211), `e1v5_r_2` (s212 s241 s243 s244 s252), `e1v5_r_3` (s254 s255 s281 s291), `e1v5_r_4` (s292 s293 s331 s341) — then `e1v5_a` and `e1v5_d`; the model alone (`bare_llm_v4`) in one run per model — `e1v5_bare_haiku`, `e1v5_bare_sonnet`, `e1v5_bare_opus`, `e1v5_bare_fable` (Opus and Fable never at the same time). Threads 6,12, repeats 5, speed check ON; one commit for every run. **Outcomes per trial** (as E1-final): race-free FASTER against the sequential original of the SAME layout; unusable (BROKEN, racy, slower, not compiling); a verified-correct program that does not finish is reported apart (4 Oct). A parallel program is race-free only where `race_check.py` finds it clean — run on every model-alone parallel program and, as the positive control, on every parallel program of the agent (`e1v5_race_check`). **Tests, class R, paired by loop over the 18 loops** (`main_comparison_stats.py e1v5_r_1..4:default_v4+discopop_gate_v4 e1v5_bare_<model>:bare_llm_v4 --three-way default_v4 --bare bare_llm_v4 --baseline-arm discopop_gate_v4 --races …`, once per model; `e1f_tests.py` for the nine): (T1, H1) the agent against DiscoPoP alone — Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-loop medians, one-sided, Cliff's delta, bootstrap interval of the median ratio; (T2–T5, H13) the agent against each model alone — per-loop unusable rate, Wilcoxon one-sided (the agent fewer); (T6–T9, reach) the agent against each model alone — per-loop race-free FASTER rate, Wilcoxon one-sided (the agent more). Holm over T1–T9 inside E1-v5; they join the campaign family beside E1-final's nine (M = 41 + 9 = 50). (H2) the agent's unusable programs: a count with every case named, no p-value — expected 0 (Fix 104 is in force). **Controls, descriptive:** class A — the agent's speed-up ÷ DiscoPoP alone's per loop (no harm if ≥ 0.9); class D — every valid trial declines. **Exclusions, fixed now:** a trial whose model call failed (`llm_call_failures`) is re-run, never counted; a trial in which a file other than the benchmark's differs (SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED — not possible by construction) is redone as Fix 103 says and, if it stays, counted unusable; nothing else is dropped. **Expectations, written before the smoke run** (E1-final: the agent 65 of 90 race-free FASTER with 1 unusable; Haiku alone 40 with 47 unusable; Sonnet 78 / 9; Opus 89 / 1; Fable 90 / 0): T1 rejected; H2 holds; T2 (against Haiku alone) rejected; T3–T5 and T6–T9 open against the strong models — on these loops the dependences are in plain sight, and a strong model alone reached as far as the agent in E1-final; the clean file is, if anything, EASIER for a model alone (no repetition loop to mishandle), so the models alone are expected at E1-final's level or above; the agent is expected at or above its 65 (three loops no longer carry a false order). **What decides what:** as E1-final — a strong model alone that reaches as far as the agent with no more unusable programs is reported as such, and the claim is the narrowed one (the pipeline makes a small model safe and beats DiscoPoP alone; where the deciding fact is hidden — E2-v5 — only the agent with evidence finds it). **Secondary, descriptive, no test:** E1-v5 against E1-final per loop (two things changed at once, so no cause is claimed), with `s212`, `s243`, `s244` named — the loops whose order sentence was false in E1-final; the sequential original's time per loop in both layouts beside every speedup of `s243`, `s244`, `s292`.
